speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your current condition, could you describe the severity and location of your flank pain, and have you noticed any changes in your urine color or frequency?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you experience any burning sensation during urination, nausea, or vomiting along with the fever? I also need to know if you have a history of kidney stones or urinary tract infections.

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you experience any burning sensation during urination, nausea, or vomiting along with the fever? I also need to know if you have a history of kidney stones or urinary tract infections.

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of a rash after amoxicillin followed by fever, flank pain, and fatigue despite switching antibiotics, I am concerned about acute interstitial nephritis. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis_with_Eosinophils

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis shows leukocyturia. Cytospin stained with Hansel’s solution reveals 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm (consistent with eosinophils). Bacterial culture is negative.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of eosinophils in your urine, combined with the history of a drug-induced rash and subsequent fever and flank pain, strongly suggests acute interstitial nephritis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis
